topic_ko: 비언어적 신호가 감정·의미를 드러내 대면 상황에서 숨기기 어려움
_note: 빈칸(논설문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab의 밑줄 어구, blank의 blank_target은 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재.

passage: Speakers do not always express everything that matters to them through words.
Nonverbal signals — changes in tone, eye contact, facial expressions, and gestures — often reveal more about a speaker's meaning than speech alone.
Because nonverbal cues can be easily misread, attentive listeners ask clarifying questions to check their understanding.
Research suggests that more than half of a speaker's message is delivered through nonverbal channels.
Failing to pay attention to these channels means losing much of the intended communication.
As Freud observed, even a silent person betrays their inner thoughts through gestures and subtle bodily signals.
In a face-to-face setting, it is therefore nearly impossible to keep one's true feelings and intentions hidden.
Skilled communicators take advantage of this by reading both words and bodies simultaneously.
choices: the role of verbal clarity in preventing misunderstandings during group discussions
the inevitable revelation of meaning and feeling through nonverbal communication
why professional speakers use body language to appear more convincing
how culture shapes the way people interpret facial expressions
the benefits of nonverbal training programs for effective leadership
theme.explanation_ko: 비언어적 신호가 의미와 감정을 자동으로 드러내므로 대면 상황에서 숨기기가 사실상 불가능하다는 내용이다. '비언어 소통을 통한 의미·감정의 불가피한 노출'인 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①언어적 명확성, ③설득력을 위한 연사의 전략, ④문화와 표정 해석, ⑤비언어 훈련 프로그램은 본문의 핵심과 다르다.

passage: Words are only part of what speakers communicate.
Tone, gaze, facial movements, and gestures carry meaning that words alone cannot fully express.
In fact, researchers estimate that the majority of a message travels through nonverbal pathways.
Even when someone stays completely silent, their body sends signals to attentive observers.
Freud captured this truth: betrayal seeps through every pore, even when lips are shut.
A simple clarifying question can reveal how much unspoken meaning listeners have already absorbed.
In a face-to-face group, these constant signals make concealment virtually impossible.
The body, it turns out, is always speaking — whether we want it to or not.
choices: How to Master the Art of Public Speaking
Words Are Just the Surface: The Power of Nonverbal Signals
Why Listening Skills Are More Important Than Speaking Skills
Silence as a Communication Strategy in Group Discussions
Building Trust Through Eye Contact and Facial Expressions
title.explanation_ko: 말은 의사소통의 표면일 뿐, 비언어 신호가 실제 의미와 감정을 끊임없이 전달한다는 내용을 담은 ②가 제목으로 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①공개 연설 기술, ③청취 대 말하기 비교, ④집단 토론에서 침묵 전략, ⑤눈 맞춤을 통한 신뢰 구축은 본문 핵심과 다르다.

passage: Speakers do not always put everything that is important to them into words.
Very often you can understand a speaker's meaning by observing their nonverbal behaviors such as a change in a vocal tone or volume, eye contact, facial expressions and gestures.
As it is easy to misinterpret nonverbal behavior, effective listeners verbally confirm their interpretations of someone's nonverbal communication.
A question as simple as "Do your nods indicate a yes vote?" can make sure that everyone is on the same wavelength.
If, as nonverbal research indicates, more than half of a speaker's meaning is conveyed nonverbally, we miss important information if failing to listen to nonverbal behavior.
Even Freud suggested that he that has eyes to see and ears to hear may convince himself that no mortal can keep a secret.
If his lips are silent, he chatters with his fingertips; betrayal oozes out of him at every pore.
No wonder it is difficult for most people to conceal what they mean and feel in a face-to-face group discussion.
grammar.explanation_ko: ③ 앞의 조건절 'if'에 이어지는 절에는 주어+동사가 필요하다. 'failing to listen'은 분사구로 주어 없이 쓰여 어법상 틀리다 → 'if we fail to listen'으로 고쳐야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①by + 동명사(observing) 수단 표현 ②it is easy to부정사 가주어 구문의 to misinterpret ④주격 관계대명사 that has ⑤간접의문문 what they mean 모두 어법상 옳다.

passage: Speakers do not always put everything that is important to them into words.
Very often you can grasp a speaker's meaning by noticing their nonverbal behaviors such as changes in vocal tone, eye contact, facial expressions and gestures.
Because nonverbal behavior is easy to misinterpret, effective listeners verbally confirm their understanding of someone's nonverbal communication.
A simple question like "Do your nods indicate a yes vote?" can ensure that everyone is on the same wavelength.
If more than half of a speaker's meaning is conveyed nonverbally, we lose vital information if we overlook nonverbal behavior.
Even Freud argued that no mortal can keep a secret: if silent, one chatters with one's fingertips.
Betrayal seeps out of a person at every pore, betraying their true feelings involuntarily.
No wonder it is difficult for most people to expose what they mean and feel in a face-to-face group discussion.
vocab.explanation_ko: ⑤ 글 전체는 비언어 신호가 감정·의미를 저절로 드러내므로 '숨기기(conceal)'가 어렵다는 내용이다. expose(드러내다)는 '숨기다'의 반대 의미이므로 문맥상 틀리다 → conceal로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①grasp(파악하다), ②indicate(나타내다), ③overlook(간과하다), ④seeps(스며 나오다) 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: Speakers do not always express everything that matters to them through words.
Very often, a speaker's meaning can be read from nonverbal cues such as tone shifts, eye contact, facial expressions, and gestures.
Because these cues can be misread, careful listeners verbally check their interpretations to stay on the same wavelength.
Research shows that more than half of a speaker's meaning travels through nonverbal channels.
Ignoring nonverbal behavior therefore means losing a large portion of the intended message.
Freud noted that even a person who stays silent betrays their inner world through gestures and subtle physical signals.
No wonder it is difficult for most people to conceal what they mean and feel in a face-to-face group discussion.
The body, in short, keeps speaking long after the mouth falls silent.
blank.blank_target: conceal what they mean and feel
choices: express themselves in a clear and logical manner
conceal what they mean and feel
follow the flow of an academic conversation
recall the nonverbal signals they observed
agree with the opinions of other group members
blank.explanation_ko: 앞에서 비언어 신호가 감정·의미를 자동으로 드러낸다(Freud 인용 포함)고 했고 마지막 문장도 '침묵해도 몸이 계속 말한다'로 이어진다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '자신이 의미하고 느끼는 것을 숨기기'(②)가 들어가야 한다.
blank.distractor_ko: ①명확하게 표현하기, ③학문적 대화 흐름 따르기, ④비언어 신호 회상, ⑤의견 동의는 본문이 말하는 '숨기기의 어려움'과 무관하다.

order.given: Speakers do not always put everything that is important to them into words. Very often you can understand a speaker's meaning by observing their nonverbal behaviors such as changes in vocal tone, eye contact, facial expressions, and gestures.

blocks.A: Even Freud suggested that no mortal can keep a secret: if silent, one chatters with one's fingertips, and betrayal oozes out at every pore. No wonder most people find it difficult to conceal what they mean and feel in a face-to-face group discussion.
blocks.B: Because nonverbal cues are easy to misinterpret, effective listeners verbally confirm their understanding. A simple question such as "Do your nods mean yes?" can ensure everyone shares the same interpretation.
blocks.C: As nonverbal research shows, more than half of a speaker's meaning is conveyed nonverbally. Failing to attend to these signals means missing a large share of the intended message.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글(비언어 행동 관찰) 뒤에 (B)에서 오해 가능성과 구두 확인 전략을 제시하고, (C)에서 '절반 이상'의 연구 수치로 중요성을 강조한 뒤, (A)에서 프로이트 인용과 결론(숨기기 어렵다)으로 마무리한다. (B)-(C)-(A).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 'No wonder'로 시작하는 결론 문장은 (B)(C)의 논거를 모두 받아야 하므로 마지막에 와야 한다.

insert.insert_sentence: If, as nonverbal research indicates, more than half of a speaker's meaning is conveyed nonverbally, we are missing a lot of important information if we fail to listen to nonverbal behavior.

passage_marked.text: Speakers do not always put everything that is important to them into words.

As it is easy to misinterpret nonverbal behavior, effective listeners verbally confirm their interpretations.
A simple clarifying question can make sure that everyone is on the same wavelength.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장('화자 의미의 절반 이상이 비언어적으로 전달됨'이라는 연구 수치)은 비언어 행동의 중요성을 수치로 강화하는 근거이다. ④ 앞 단순한 확인 질문 예시 직후에 놓여 '왜 그 질문이 중요한가'를 수치로 뒷받침하고, ⑤의 결론(숨기기 어렵다)으로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.
insert.distractor_ko: ①②③에 삽입하면 연구 수치가 실용 전략 소개 이전에 등장해 흐름이 어색하고, ⑤에 삽입하면 결론문 뒤에 근거가 오는 역순이 된다.

passage: Speakers do not always express what matters to them in words.
Nonverbal cues such as tone, eye contact, and gestures often reveal a speaker's true meaning.
Effective listeners verbally verify their readings of such cues to avoid misunderstanding.
Research shows that more than half of a speaker's meaning is transmitted through nonverbal channels.
Freud observed that even silence betrays inner thoughts: the body keeps speaking through gestures and pores.
No wonder concealing one's true feelings and intentions in a face-to-face group discussion is so difficult.
Nonverbal behavior is not optional background noise — it is the primary carrier of authentic meaning.
To truly understand another person, one must learn to listen beyond words.
summary.summary_template: Because more than half of communication is __(A)__, people inevitably __(B)__ their true feelings and meaning through body language in face-to-face settings, making concealment extremely difficult.
summary.explanation_ko: 의사소통의 절반 이상이 (A)nonverbal(비언어적)이기 때문에 사람들은 대면 상황에서 자신의 진짜 감정·의미를 몸짓으로 (B)reveal(드러내게) 되어 숨기기가 극히 어렵다. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 verbal(②⑤)이나 emotional(④)이 아니라 nonverbal, (B)는 hide(②)나 control(③)이 아니라 reveal이어야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 효과적인 청자는 누군가의 비언어적 의사소통에 대한 자신의 해석을 구두로 확인한다.
writing.answer: Effective listeners verbally confirm their interpretations of someone's nonverbal communication.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Effective listeners + 부사 verbally + 동사 confirm + 목적어 their interpretations of someone's nonverbal communication.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 대부분의 사람들이 대면 집단 토론에서 자신이 의미하고 느끼는 것을 숨기기가 어렵다는 것은 당연하다.
writing.answer: No wonder it is difficult for most people to conceal what they mean and feel in a face-to-face group discussion.
writing.explanation_ko: No wonder + 가주어 it + is difficult + for most people + to부정사(conceal) + 간접의문절(what they mean and feel) + 장소 부사구.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 비언어적 행동을 오해하기 쉽기 때문에, 효과적인 청자는 누군가의 비언어적 의사소통에 대한 자신의 해석을 구두로 확인한다.
conditions: 이유의 접속사 As와 가주어 it 구문을 사용할 것
writing.answer: As it is easy to misinterpret nonverbal behavior, effective listeners verbally confirm their interpretations of someone's nonverbal communication.
writing.explanation_ko: As it is easy to V(~하기 쉽기 때문에) 가주어 구문 + verbally confirm(구두로 확인하다) + their interpretations of ~.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: If, as nonverbal research indicates, more than half of a speaker's meaning is conveyed nonverbally, we are missing a lot of important information if we fail to "listen" to nonverbal behavior.
writing.answer: 만약 비언어적 연구가 나타내듯 화자 의미의 절반 이상이 비언어적으로 전달된다면, 비언어적 행동을 '듣는' 것에 실패한다면 우리는 많은 중요한 정보를 놓치고 있는 것이다.
writing.explanation_ko: 삽입된 as절(비언어 연구가 나타내듯) / more than half ~ is conveyed nonverbally(수동태 조건절) / fail to listen(~을 듣는 데 실패하다).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Because nonverbal signals constantly (A)___________ a speaker's true meaning and feelings, most people find it very hard to (B)___________ what they mean and feel in a face-to-face group discussion.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 비언어 신호는 의미를 끊임없이 '전달한다(convey)' — 본문 5번 문장에 등장. (B) 따라서 자신의 의미·감정을 '숨기기(conceal)' 어렵다 — 본문 마지막 문장의 핵심어.

writing.context: Even Freud suggested that 'he that has eyes to see and ears to hear may convince himself that no mortal can keep a secret. If his lips are silent, he chatters with his fingertips; ___________ oozes out of him at every pore.'
writing.explanation_ko: 프로이트 인용의 마지막 구에서 '배반(betrayal)'이 모든 모공에서 스며 나온다고 묘사하며 비언어 신호의 불가피성을 표현한다.
